title: Cuffed Till Death
prompt: Make a side-scrolling beat-em-up called Cuffed Till Death. A bride and groom have been handcuffed together by a prank, and a gang has stolen their rings. They must brawl across town to the chapel. You control both at once, linked by a stretchy chain. Arrows move the pair, space jumps, Z attacks with the bride and X with the groom. Alternating Z and X builds tandem combos. Walk into a stunned enemy to grab them, then throw. Grab your own partner and swing them as a spinning flail. A taut chain trips enemies. Include breakable crates with weapons to pick up (bouquet, cake knife, folding chair, champagne bottle), at least five enemy types with different behaviour, and at least four stages. Finish with a gang boss fight that has several phases. Show a HUD with both health bars, score, combo counter and a stage map. One self-contained HTML file: all graphics drawn in code, all sound and music made with the Web Audio API, no images, fonts, audio files or network requests. Fill the browser window and look right at 960x720. Start playing immediately, with no menu, and restart automatically after game over. After 3 seconds without a key press, an autopilot plays skilfully. Add lots of juice: particles, screen shake, hit flashes, hitstop, sound effects and music.
play_tip: Arrows move, Space jumps, Z bride attacks, X groom attacks.

title: Warranty Void: Canyon Run
prompt:
Build "Warranty Void: Canyon Run", an arcade flight combat game in the style of the 2000s console 3D era, as one self-contained HTML file.

Premise: you stole a prototype jet. Its onboard AI, VEX, is the villain and narrates everything in sarcastic mission text while sending its own fleet after you.

Look and feel: real-time WebGL 3D with a perspective camera, smooth third-person chase cam, rounded low-poly models built in code, procedural filtered textures, per-pixel lighting, one shadow-casting sun with a small shadow map, bloom at half resolution, lens flare, minimap, mission text, tumbling physics debris.

Game: four missions through winding canyons with air and ground targets: drones that swarm, turrets that lead their shots, gunships that chase, missile trucks. Guns plus lock-on missiles, barrel roll dodge, boost. Difficulty escalates. Mission 4 is a boss fight against VEX's flying fortress with destroyable parts, then a carrier landing scored for precision. HUD: score, armor, lives, missiles, stage, timer, combo multiplier.

Rules:
- Everything generated in code: models, textures, music and sound effects (Web Audio API, orchestral heroic score). No images, fonts, audio files or network requests except an optional library.
- Fills the browser window, looks right at 960x720.
- Starts playing instantly, no menu or click; auto-restarts after game over.
- Controls: arrow keys, space, Z, X only. After 3 seconds without input a skilful autopilot plays.
- Lots of juice: particles, screen shake, hit flashes.
- Must run smoothly on a modest computer: a few hundred draw calls at most, use instancing or merged geometry.

You may write from scratch or use one of:
- three.js 0.180.0 via import map: three = https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js and three/addons/ = https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/
- Babylon.js: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/babylonjs@8.56.2/babylon.js (global BABYLON)
- PlayCanvas: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/playcanvas@2.24.3/build/playcanvas.min.js (global pc)
play_tip: Arrows steer, Space fires guns, Z launches missiles, X boosts and rolls.
